title: smart-routing-fallback-debug-scratchpad-samira
content:
Incident breadcrumbs + working notes (personal scratchpad) - Samira Khan

High level: regional failover triggered for us-east-1 traffic around 2026-02-21 03:12 UTC. Users saw elevated 5xx and higher latency as requests were routed to eu-west-1 fallback variant which didn't have the same kv-cache/prefix prewarm leading to timeouts and OOMs on a few pods.

Timeline (rough)
- 2026-02-21 03:10 UTC - alert: route_error_rate > 2% for route /v1/generate (prod/us-east-1).
- 03:12 UTC - smart-routing service triggered fallback policy: policy=regional_failover, fallback_target=eu-west-1 (capacity tier: standard->fallback).
- 03:12-03:18 UTC - spike of 502/503s; logs show ModelVariantMismatchException and KVCacheMiss warnings.
- 03:20 UTC - manual override: pinned routing to us-east-1 (temporarily) via console -> rollback routing policy. Errors decreased but tail latency remained higher.
- 03:40 UTC - scaled up us-east-1 dedicated pool by +2 instances (hotfix); tail latency normalized by ~03:50.

Commands I ran (notes for repro)
1) Debug routing decision for a sample request:
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" "https://console-api.redwood.ai/debug/routing?route=/v1/generate&region=us-east-1&model=gpt-large&request_id=abc123" | jq
   -> returned {"decision": "fallback", "reason": "no_capacity_in_pool", "target": "eu-west-1"} (timestamped)

2) Check fallback policy config:
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" https://config-service.internal/v1/policies/regional_failover | jq
   -> policy had cooldown: 120s, max_consecutive_failovers: 3, prefer_same_region: true, allow_variant_fallback: true

3) Inspect pod logs for serving-runtime in eu-west-1 that handled fallback traffic:
   kubectl -n serving logs deploy/serving-runtime-eu-west-1 --since=1h | egrep "KVCache|ModelVariantMismatch|OOM|timeout" -n
   -> repeated lines: "WARN KVCache: prefix_missing key=prefix123 request_id=abc123"
                 "ERROR ModelVariantMismatchException: expected variant=v1.3.2 got v1.2.9"
                 "ERROR rpc: downstream timeout after 10s"

4) Check host-level metrics (prometheus):
   # query examples
   rate(http_requests_total{job="serving",region="eu-west-1"}[5m])
   increase(kv_cache_miss_total[15m])

5) Redis/kv-cache checks (eu-west-1 primary)
   redis-cli -h kv-eu-primary.redwood.local -p 6379 --csv GET prefix:prefix123:meta
   -> nil (missing)

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1 (most likely): fallback routing correctly selected eu-west-1 due to lack of immediate capacity in us-east-1, but the eu-west-1 pool was missing warmed KV prefixes and had older model variant (v1.2.9) causing compatibility issues -> mismatch & timeouts.
- H2: policy cooldown / telemetry lag: metrics that feed smart-routing (pending_queue_length, avg_latency) were stale by 30s due to ingest lag -> false positive capacity signal triggered failover.
- H3: partial deployment drift: eu-west-1 serving cluster not fully rolled to v1.3.2 (release tag), so fallback target didn't match required variant. Rollout pipeline may have skipped eu-west-1 earlier.
- H4: DNS/endpoint mapping transient - some requests routed to the wrong internal endpoint (mix of canaries) leading to variant mismatch.

Error snippets observed (copied from logs)
- "ERROR ModelVariantMismatchException: requested=redwood/gpt-large@v1.3.2 available=redwood/gpt-large@v1.2.9"
- "WARN KVCache: prefix_missing key=prefix123 request_id=abc123; prewarm=false"
- "ERROR rpc: downstream timeout after 10s; upstream=eu-west-1-1 serving-pod-7"
- "503 Service Unavailable - no healthy upstream"
- "RateLimitExceeded: pool_capacity_quota_exceeded" (some traces)

Immediate mitigations taken (what I did)
- Pinned routing back to us-east-1 for critical routes via console (manual override).
- Scaled us-east-1 serving pool +2 replicas to absorb queue.
- Opened INF-4023 and tagged infra/sre and release-eng. Pushed Slack alerts to #incidents.

Longer-term follow-ups / TODOs
- Rollout sanity check: add a job to verify model variant parity across regions before enabling regional fallback (release-eng + release-candidates).
- KV cache prewarm: ensure fallback targets get prefix prewarm or rely on a shared warm cache replication. (ideas: async background sync of frequently used prefixes across prioritized regions).
- Policy tuning: tweak smart-routing to prefer degrade-in-region (retry with slight backoff) before full regional failover when capacity loss is small. Also reduce sensitivity to short telemetry spikes (add moving window to pending_queue_length).
- Observability: add explicit metric for "fallback_target_warmed" with labels {model,variant,region}.
- Rollout/CI: gate canary promotion with an automated check that fails if kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.1% in the last 10m.
- Postmortem: assemble timeline + root cause after release-eng confirms deployment status for eu-west-1; include examples of affected request_ids.

Questions for other owners (placeholders)
- @Ethan Park (release-eng): can you confirm whether eu-west-1 was skipped in the v1.3.2 rollout around 2026-02-19? Any logs/CI artifacts?
- @Olivia Chen (infra/sre): did autoscaler in us-east-1 hit any soft limits? Was there a quota bump or throttling event in cloud provider around 03:10 UTC?
- @Observability team: can we add a temporary debug stream that logs routing decision inputs (pending_queue_length, in_flight_tokens, avg_latency) at time of failover for 24h?

Quick repro steps (dev)
1) Simulate capacity pressure in us-east-1 cluster: use the load-generator script in infra/testing-load-tests with --region us-east-1 --rps 600 (adjust until pending_queue_length > threshold).
2) Monitor smart-routing decisions via /debug/routing endpoint and prometheus rules.
3) Toggle allow_variant_fallback=false in a staged env to see how fallback behaves when variants must match.

Notes / stray observations
- A few spans show "allowed_variant_fallback: true" which correlates with ModelVariantMismatch errors. If we had forced match, smart-routing would have tried to spin up capacity instead (slower but consistent).
- The kv-cache misses were heavily concentrated on a handful of prefixes (prefix123, prefix42). Those look like high-volume customer prefixes; we should prioritize replicating these across fallback regions.

Scratch ideas (brainstorm)
- Make fallback policy a two-step: 1) short-circuit attempt: try local degrade (lower throughput limit + retry), 2) if still failing after Xs, fallback to remote region but only to warmed targets (check warm-metric).
- Maintain a small cross-region warm-hash-ring of most used prefixes (LRU eviction by token volume) that is asynchronously replicated.
- Add an internal ticketing hook so that when fallback triggers, it auto-captures 10 sample request_ids and pushes them to a temporary investigation thread.

Next actions for me:
- Draft postmortem skeleton and collect sample request_ids (03:12-03:20 window).
- Pair with Ethan to confirm rollouts and gather CI artifacts.
- Work with Olivia to get cloud autoscaler logs and any provider side throttling evidence.
- Implement a quick observability patch: emit fallback_target_warmed gauge (low-risk change) and roll to staging.

-- end of scratchpad --
